analysis:
Examined base_text units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, base lines 1756-3038. These cover ready-receipt monotonicity, the no-ready failure matrix, write-behind barriers (low disk, ENOSPC, close, queue drop), staging reservations (endAdoption/completeStaging/abandon, shared-entry single reservation, deadline refusal), kv3 root isolation and whole-root maintenance (TTL, global budget, epoch retention). All of this is unchanged test code: the file_changes range map is complete, and base changed ranges are empty.

The only change is a head-side addition at lines 3140-3240. It adds tests asserting that the whole-root maintainer remembers a header-ownership verdict only for unchanged files. A header corrupted after an earlier pass, with its mtime restored and only ctime changed, must lose ownership: filesSeen==0, and the file is not deleted. The patch excerpt also shows a test that a malformed lookalike replaced by a valid block is owned on the next pass. That head text is outside these units and the excerpt is truncated.

This bears on T-041(b): the maintainer must not unlink files it cannot prove it owns, and must not treat stale cached verdicts as ownership. The added tests strengthen rather than weaken that property. No production source is in this batch, so I cannot verify that SSDWholeRootMaintainer actually keys its verdict cache on ctime/inode/size.

Integration should check the production change to SSDWholeRootMaintainer, which is presumably elsewhere in the PR:
- The verdict cache must be invalidated on any change to inode, size, mtime or ctime.
- Cached verdicts must not cause deletion of non-owned files.
- Header verification must not follow symlinks (SSDNoFollowIO).
- The cache must be bounded in memory.

Test-only changes introduce no runtime attack surface.
